answer.decision: Adopt continuous database log backups with weekly full backups, retain 12 monthly recovery points, tier older backups to cold storage, and perform regular restore tests.
answer.action: Configure transaction-log capture at intervals safely below 15 minutes; create weekly full backups; preserve month-end recoverability for 12 months; move eligible older fulls, logs, and monthly recovery points to cold storage; keep recent recovery chains hot; run quarterly restore drills and monitor measured RPO, RTO, retrieval delay, and monthly cost until the 35% savings target is verified.
reasons: Continuous logs can satisfy the database RPO of at most 15 minutes when captured frequently enough.
A weekly-full-plus-logs restore completed in 76 minutes, leaving 44 minutes within the two-hour RTO for cold-tier retrieval and operational variance.
Compliance requires 12 months of month-end recoverability, not 12 months of daily full images, so daily full retention is unnecessary.
Daily full database backups produce 72% of current backup storage cost, making reduced full-backup frequency the strongest cost lever.
Cold storage costs 68% less per GB, so tiering older recovery points provides additional savings toward the required 35% reduction.
A universal 30-day retention policy would violate the 12-month month-end recoverability requirement, while merely negotiating pricing does not demonstrate the required savings.
assumptions: Continuous logs are retained with every dependent weekly full so each required recovery point remains usable.
The 76-minute restore drill is representative of production database size and recovery procedures.
Cold-tier retrieval can occur within its stated 20-minute maximum and still preserve the two-hour RTO.
The final storage model, including log growth and retained month-end recovery chains, confirms at least 35% monthly savings before the old policy is retired.
risks: Broken or missing log chains could prevent point-in-time recovery.
Database growth or restore contention could push recovery beyond the tested 76 minutes.
Cold-tier retrieval delays or service degradation could threaten the RTO margin.
Log storage, weekly-full retention, or minimum-storage charges could reduce savings below 35% unless measured before rollout.
Deleting legacy daily fulls before validating restores and compliance coverage could create unrecoverable gaps.

citations.claim: The policy must achieve database RPO of at most 15 minutes, RTO of at most two hours, and at least 35% lower monthly backup storage cost.
Daily full database backups account for 72% of current backup storage cost.
Point-in-time recovery logs average 6% of a daily full backup's storage per day.
Compliance requires 12 months of month-end recoverability but does not require daily full images.
A weekly-full-plus-logs restore drill completed in 76 minutes.
Cold-tier storage costs 68% less per GB and can add up to 20 minutes of retrieval delay.
The database backup policy is the dominant remaining cost lever because document objects already use lifecycle tiering.
